items.title: NUBE-MCBA dispute: Ramanan's appeal to continue for court ruling on legal issues, says ministry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The continuation of Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan's appeal in the dispute between the National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) and the Malaysian Commercial Banks' Association (MCBA) is aimed at obtaining a Court of Appeal ruling on legal issues arising from the High Court's decision, the ministry said today. "However, MCBA exercised its right to apply for a stay of execution of the High Court's decision, and the application was granted by the Court," the ministry said. However, on Sept 26, the High Court allowed MCBA's application to stay the execution of the decision pending the association's appeal at the Court of Appeal.

items.title: Woman arrested after driver swap precedes PLUS crash that killed retired cop, wife near Kuala Muda
items.summary: Police are investigating whether the woman, who owns the Perodua Bezza, was driving or a passenger when the crash occurred on the North-South Expressway near Kuala Muda yesterday. According to Sinar Harian , Kuala Muda district police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said the woman was detained to help establish the circumstances surrounding the collision. The crash occurred at about noon at KM114.4 of the expressway, killing retired police sergeant Suhaimi Saidin, 64, and his wife Normah Hashim, 60.

items.title: Musk's futuristic Cybertruck rolls towards exit
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Production of Cybertrucks — the pickups hailed by enthusiasts as a symbol of Elon Musk's futuristic ambitions and equally hated as ugly reminders of the Donald Trump era — will wind down, the Tesla chief executive said on Friday. Tesla will stop building the truck at its Texas factory around the middle of 2027 to free up space for its Cybercab robotaxi, Musk said. "Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production," Musk wrote on X. Musk did not say whether the truck would be built elsewhere or discontinued altogether, nor what would happen to outstanding orders.

items.title: Palestinian PM’s adviser calls for deeper Malaysia cooperation in development, diplomacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Palestine hopes to deepen cooperation with Malaysia through concrete projects and programmes to support the country’s development and economy towards the realisation of the State of Palestine, Advisor to the Palestinian Prime Minister for International Relations Izzat Abdel Hadi said. “Malaysia can also assist through humanitarian support, particularly in Gaza, including healthcare, education and community infrastructure,” he said during an interview on Bernama TV’s The Nation programme, Palestine Beyond The Headlines: Rebuilding Under Occupation , recently. Abdel Hadi said Malaysia’s standing within Asean and the international community could also help amplify Palestinian concerns and strengthen diplomatic support for Palestinian rights and statehood.

items.title: Dozens of pilot whales stranded on New Zealand coast
items.summary: SYDNEY: Dozens of pilot whales have been found stranded on a beach on New Zealand's North Island, and rescuers are trying to refloat a handful of survivors, the country's conservation department said on Thursday. At least 20 pilot whales were stranded along the Ngawi coast near Cape Palliser, the southernmost point of the North Island, the Department of Conservation said. Locals said up to 50 whales had been stranded along the coastline overnight, Radio New Zealand reported.

items.title: Saifullizan Ishak named new Sarawak police chief, Zailanni Amit appointed deputy
items.summary: KUCHING, Nov 7 — DCP Saifullizan Ishak has been promoted to Commissioner of Police (CP) and appointed Sarawak’s new police chief. In a Facebook post on its official page, Polis Sarawak, the Sarawak Contingent Police Headquarters announced that DCP Zailanni Amit would replace him as Sarawak deputy police commissioner. Hailing from Kedah, Saifullizan, 56, had also held various posts throughout his 31-year service with the police since 1995 — including chief assistant director for integrity, Special Branch chief assistant director, security liaison officer for the High Commission of Malaysia in Singapore, and investigating officer.

items.title: Make halal certification compulsory for slaughterhouses, govt told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Slaughterhouse operators should be required to obtain Malaysian Halal Certification to address confusion among Muslims over the halal status of food products. The source said a proposal to make halal certification compulsory for all slaughterhouse operators, restaurant owners and food manufacturers was brought before the cabinet in 2024. He said the voluntary nature of halal certification had created confusion, particularly among Muslims, over whether food producers complied with halal requirements.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan MB expects 7,000 visitors at Deepavali Open House on Nov 14
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 7 — About 7,000 visitors are expected to attend the Negeri Sembilan-level Deepavali Open House at the Seremban City Council (MBS) Hall on November 14, from 11am to 4pm. Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the state government had also increased its allocation for this year’s Deepavali Carnival to RM70,000 from RM30,000 last year. “The state government invites all Negeri Sembilan residents to attend the Deepavali celebration in large numbers to foster goodwill among the communities.

items.title: HR Ministry: Ramanan’s appeal seeks legal clarity, not an end to NUBE-MCBA negotiations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 7 — The continuation of Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan’s appeal in the dispute between the National Union of Bank Employees (NUBE) and the Malaysian Commercial Banks’ Association (MCBA) is aimed at obtaining a Court of Appeal ruling on legal issues arising from the High Court’s decision, the ministry said today. “The human resources minister (Ramanan) did not apply for a stay of execution of the High Court’s decision, while the Department of Industrial Relations Malaysia had taken proactive steps by summoning the parties involved to resume conciliation proceedings. “However, MCBA exercised its right to apply for a stay of execution of the High Court’s decision, and the application was granted by the Court,” Kesuma said.

items.title: Fahmi: Malaysia eyes shift in internet coverage measurements to include key economic areas
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 7 — Malaysia intends to propose at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) level that internet coverage measurements should no longer focus solely on the Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) standard, but should also take into account areas where economic activities take place. He said the existing approach, which is based on coverage in populated areas, should be reconsidered by taking into account the concept of Coverage of Economic Areas to ensure that connectivity needs in economic areas were also given due attention. Fahmi said areas that warranted attention included major roads, railway lines, ports, coastal areas used by fishermen, as well as tourism and recreational destinations.

items.title: "I am still the menteri besar,' says Ismail amid replacement speculation
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has declined to comment on speculation that he would be replaced by Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias. "As of today, I am still the menteri besar," he said briefly after attending the Little India Deepavali Bazaar Carnival last night. Meanwhile, Ismail said the state government had allocated RM70,000 for the Little India Deepavali Bazaar Carnival, which included contributions to the Indian community in rural areas.

items.title: LTAT launches five-year anti-corruption plan to safeguard military retirement funds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) yesterday launched its Ethics, Transparency, Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy (SETIA) 2026-2030 to strengthen good governance practices and ensure the sustainability of the retirement funds of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel. According to LTAT, SETIA marks the next phase in its ongoing efforts to strengthen institutional integrity, enhance accountability and foster ethical practices across all aspects of its operations and investment decisions. The launch ceremony, held in conjunction with the 2026 International Anti-Corruption Day celebrations, was attended by LTAT Chairman Gen (Rtd) Tan Sri Azizan Ariffin, LTAT Chief Executive Datuk Mohammad Ashraf Md Radzi, Deputy Secretary-General of the Treasury and LTAT Integrity Committee Chairman Datuk Shahrazat Ahmad, and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Community Education Division director Datuk Hairuzam Mohmad Amin @ Hamim.

items.title: Puncak Alam's rapid development brings flooding, traffic woes
items.summary: KUALA SELANGOR: Rapid growth in Bandar Puncak Alam, also known as Bandar Shah Alam 2, has outpaced infrastructure development, leaving its nearly 250,000 residents grappling with mounting problems. However, essential infrastructure has yet to be upgraded, raising concerns among residents. Puncak Alam Residents' chairman Mohd Hanif Md Sultan said residents were concerned that infrastructure development had fallen behind despite the township's rapid growth and numerous high-impact projects.

items.title: Shaharul is new Pahang police chief, 18 others transferred
items.summary: "Sarawak Deputy Police Commissioner Deputy Commissioner Saifullizan Ishak has been appointed Sarawak police commissioner with the acting rank of commissioner of police," he said in a statement. Meanwhile, Pahang Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Datuk Mohd Yusri Othman has been appointed Penang deputy police chief with the acting rank of deputy commissioner. [[nid:1572618]] "Penang Criminal Investigation Department chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Zailanni Amit has been appointed Sarawak deputy police commissioner with the acting rank of deputy commissioner," he said.

items.title: Boy, 11, drowns after falling into river while fishing with friends in Subang Perdana
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — A group of children’s joyful fishing outing in a river near Desa Subang Perantau 2, Subang Perdana here ended in tragedy when one of them was found drowned yesterday afternoon. Selangor Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the victim who died was an 11-year-old Indonesian boy. “The search operation for the victim was also assisted by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) from BBP Pelabuhan Klang and BBP Shah Alam.

items.title: Malaysia, Austria seek closer ties ahead of 65 years of diplomatic relations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Austria and Malaysia are committed to further strengthening bilateral relations in various fields, including foreign policy, regional cooperation, trade, investment, education, and culture, as both countries prepare to celebrate 65 years of diplomatic relations next year. Austrian Ambassador to Malaysia Gerhard Eisl said the two countries shared common values and were like-minded partners on various international issues, particularly in promoting peace, dialogue, multilateralism, and international cooperation. “Malaysia is an important partner for Austria.

items.title: One dead, six injured in Proton Ertiga–Honda Civic collision in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 7 — An elderly man was killed while six others sustained minor injuries in a collision involving a Proton Ertiga multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) and a Honda Civic at Jalan Ladang Sindora towards Ulu Belitong, Renggam here yesterday afternoon. Renggam Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Ramli Said said the department received an emergency call at 3.38pm and dispatched six firefighters and a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT) to the scene. “Three other occupants of the Proton Ertiga, aged between eight and 54, sustained minor injuries, while the Honda Civic driver and two passengers, who were family members, also sustained minor injuries.

items.title: MACC looking for Toh Lean Seng, 53, to assist in money laundering investigation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is seeking a local man to assist in a money laundering investigation. The MACC said the individual, identified as Toh Lean Seng, is 53 years old, adding that efforts to locate the man at his last known address at 15-1 231, TR Service Apartment, 231 Jalan Tun Razak, 50490 Kuala Lumpur, were unsuccessful. “Anyone who knows or has information about this individual is urged to contact the investigating officer, PsK Mohd Shokray Yahaya, at 019-6236680 or via email at mohdshokray@sprm.gov.my,” the commission said in a statement last night.

items.title: Penang police probe viral video alleging officers took money during roadside check
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Police are conducting a thorough investigation into a viral video circulating on social media alleging misconduct by police personnel while carrying out law enforcement duties at Puncak Erskine, Jalan Fettes, in Tanjung Tokong here. Northeast District Police Chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police detected the video yesterday following its circulation on social media, which had attracted public attention. He said the investigation would also look into whether the police personnel involved had complied with procedures and disciplinary regulations.

items.title: Landslide forces full closure of Jalan Rawang-Kuala Selangor stretch after heavy rain
items.summary: The Selangor Public Works Department (JKR) said the landslide, which occurred at 11 pm, involved failures of both the upslope and downslope, causing part of the road structure at the affected section to collapse. The agency said the landslide also brought down trees, blocking the entire road to traffic. “The road closure was implemented by the Gombak District JKR, while information on alternative routes was disseminated to road users through the Facebook pages of JKR Selangor and Gombak District JKR yesterday morning.

items.title: MMEA seizes RM8m worth of vessels, items over suspected illegal cargo transfer off Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — Two vessels and other items with an estimated total value of RM8 million were seized by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Penang waters on Thursday for allegedly carrying out cargo transfer activities without a valid licence. In a statement today, Penang MMEA director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the vessels, a tugboat and an unregistered sampan, were detained at 11.40am following information received and public complaints. He said an initial inspection found that the vessels were allegedly involved in transferring cargo from the sampan to the tugboat without a valid cargo licence as required under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance (MSO) 1952.

items.title: Malaysia seeks early date for Anwar-Prabowo talks as bilateral agreements await signing
items.summary: The upcoming 14th Annual Consultation will bring together Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Prabowo to review bilateral cooperation and discuss issues of mutual interest. Muzafar said he also conveyed greetings from the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and Anwar to Prabowo, while reaffirming Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening cooperation with Indonesia as a neighbour and strategic partner. “President Prabowo repeatedly emphasised that Malaysia and Indonesia are brotherly nations.

items.title: Deepavali Carnival at Bukit Jalil attracts nearly 200,000 visitors, gives 700 entrepreneurs business boost, says Ramanan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The 24th Deepavali Carnival at the National Stadium in Bukit Jalil near here, which attracted nearly 200,000 visitors, including foreign tourists, proves the event is not merely a festive shopping venue but also a platform to spur local businesses. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the encouraging response to the nine-day carnival, which began October 30, gave 700 entrepreneurs an opportunity to expand their market reach and boost sales. The carnival gathered various exhibitors and local entrepreneurs offering goods, food, beverages and essential items for Deepavali.

items.title: Sarawak’s education opportunities are for all races, says PBB vice-president
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 7 — Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) Vice President Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee has defended the Sarawak government’s inclusive policy of providing educational opportunities to all races, while reminding the Bumiputera community not to be left behind in seizing the opportunities provided. He said the Bumiputera community should not question the opportunities given to other races, but should instead ensure that their children take advantage of the state government’s educational and development opportunities. What we should worry about is whether our Bumiputera children are seizing those open opportunities.

items.title: ITU: Malaysia to propose expanding internet coverage to areas with economic activities
items.summary: DOHA: Malaysia intends to propose at the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) level that Internet coverage measurements should no longer focus solely on the Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) standard, but should also take into account areas where economic activities take place. He said the existing approach, which is based on coverage in populated areas, should be reconsidered by taking into account the concept of Coverage of Economic Areas to ensure that connectivity needs in economic areas were also given due attention. Fahmi said areas that warranted attention included major roads, railway lines, ports, coastal areas used by fishermen, as well as tourism and recreational destinations.

items.title: Hassan Karim urges Melaka voters to judge Pakatan on federal government track record
items.summary: He said the government led by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had a good record in governance, particularly in creating employment opportunities for the people. “Official government employment and investment statistics show that hundreds of thousands of new jobs have been and are being generated by the Madani government,” he said in an open message to Melaka voters and the public yesterday. Hassan said the government was targeting at least 30,000 new high-skilled and technology-based jobs for local youths and graduates.

items.title: Selangor Sultan marks 25-year reign with foundation to support education, community welfare
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah last night graced the official launch of Yayasan Sultan Selangor at a Royal Charity Gala Dinner held in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebrations of his reign. Also present was the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, accompanied by the Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah and his wife Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Datuk Abdul Aziz. Tengku Amir Shah said Yayasan Sultan Selangor stands on four pillars namely community welfare, education and scholarships, heritage and cultural preservation, as well as emergency assistance.

items.title: Unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses face closure, demolition under Selangor crackdown
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Selangor State Executive Council has directed all local authorities in the state to take immediate enforcement action against unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses. State Islamic Religious Affairs and Innovation Committee chairman Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the action would target premises operating without licences from local authorities and those without certified slaughterers. He said the public could check the list of halal-certified premises through the Halal Malaysia Portal at www.halal.gov.my and report any suspected unlicensed poultry slaughterhouses to the local authorities or the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais).

items.title: Singapore-based Bitdeer eyes further investment in Malaysia’s AI infrastructure, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Singapore-headquartered Bitdeer Technologies Group (Bitdeer) has expressed its intention to continue investing in Malaysia due to its confidence in the Madani government’s direction and policies on digital transformation. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was conveyed to him during a courtesy visit from Bitdeer founder, chairman and chief executive officer Jihan Wu, along with his delegation, earlier yesterday. The Nasdaq-listed company, which provides cloud computing services for artificial intelligence (AI) and Bitcoin mining infrastructure, is currently finetuning a long-term investment proposal to develop world-class AI infrastructure in Malaysia, Anwar said in a post on X.

items.title: Cop injured as tree crushes motorcycle in Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A policeman was injured when a falling tree crushed his motorcycle in front of a premises in Padang Temusu around midnight. Civil Defence Force personnel treated the man at the scene and took him to Sultan Abdul Halim Hospital. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Malaysia must speed up agricultural modernisation to strengthen food security, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Malaysia must accelerate the modernisation of its agricultural sector and improve production efficiency to strengthen food security amid growing challenges, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said Malaysia could learn from countries such as Brazil, which had significantly increased its agricultural output, particularly corn, through a market guarantee system rather than relying solely on subsidies. Recounting his meeting with his Brazilian counterpart, Mohamad said Brazil’s approach did not involve providing subsidies to farmers.

items.title: DPM Zahid: Malaysia eyes stronger defence ties with Turkiye, with focus on technology transfer
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia views its defence cooperation with Turkiye as a strategic avenue to strengthen its technological capabilities, deepen bilateral relations and contribute to regional stability in South-east Asia. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the partnership extends beyond the procurement of defence equipment to include knowledge and technology transfer, while opening up opportunities for broader cooperation in economic, technological, educational and diplomatic fields. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the rural and regional development minister, expressed strong confidence that deepened defence and technological cooperation will propel both nations toward realising their ambitious US$10 billion bilateral trade target, while creating a more balanced and vibrant trade relationship.

items.title: Malaysia, Turkiye set US$10b trade target by 2030 following Zahid-Erdogan discussions
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi paid a courtesy call on Turkiye President Recep Tayyip Erdogan here on Friday, with discussions focusing on strengthening bilateral relations and increasing Malaysia-Turkiye trade value. The 30-minute meeting, starting at 4pm local time (9pm Malaysian time), occurred shortly after Erdogan launched the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC), before Ahmad Zahid joined a session titled “Turkiye From Regional Power to Multi-Regional Actor”. Ahmad Zahid also touched on Turkiye’s role as the 12th Asean Sectoral Dialogue Partner and Malaysia’s commitment as the coordinating country for Asean-Turkiye relations to expand strategic cooperation between both parties.

items.title: Malaysia rises two spots in good governance ranking, Anwar warns against complacency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Malaysia’s rise to 40th place among 133 countries in the Chandler Good Government Index (CGGI) 2026 recognises the government’s continuous efforts to strengthen national administrative capacity, integrity and effectiveness, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the Madani government’s priority remains building robust institutions, improving public service delivery and ensuring every development effort brings tangible benefits to the people. Malaysia climbed two spots from 42nd in 2025 in the index, which evaluates national governance performance across seven core pillars.

items.title: Selangor freezes Puncak Alam development works, orders faster flood mitigation measures
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Selangor State Executive Council has decided to immediately halt all development works in Puncak Alam, Kuala Selangor, while flood mitigation plans and the Environmental Impact Assessment are reassessed. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said at the same time, the Public Works Department will temporarily close Jalan Batu Arang in Rawang following a collapsed bank to facilitate repair works. “Additionally, small and large scale flood mitigation works statewide, especially in higher-risk areas, must be expedited immediately rather than following conventional schedules, as rain is expected almost daily.

items.title: Better care support needed to keep women in the workforce
items.summary: She said one of the main challenges facing women in the country is the unequal sharing of family caregiving responsibilities, particularly for single mothers and female heads of households. Therefore, (women) empowerment policies must pay particular attention to single mothers, low-income women, those in rural areas and women working in the informal sector," she said in an interview with Bernama recently. Elaborating, Rajwani said childcare and family responsibilities significantly influence women's decisions to return to work.

items.title: Najib’s Taman Duta residence gazetted as prison, house arrest deferred pending legal clarification
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The residence of former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak on Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, has been declared a prison for the imprisonment or detention of persons in lawful custody. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, situated on Lot 5746, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, District of Kuala Lumpur. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, 50480 Kuala Lumpur, situated on Lot 5746, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, District of Kuala Lumpur, Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur, to be a prison for the purposes of the Act for the imprisonment or detention of persons in lawful custody,” the gazette stated.

items.title: Anwar open to easing foreign worker rules for sectors facing shortages, warns against exploitation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government is prepared to consider easing foreign worker approval requirements for sectors facing genuine manpower shortages, particularly the plantation sector. Anwar also said he had instructed the relevant authorities to simplify approval procedures for certain urgent labour needs. “Plantations are asking for workers.

items.title: Bank Rakyat website experiences temporary disruption [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Rakyat's corporate portal is reportedly experiencing a temporary access disruption. Bank Rakyat, through a notification on its official Facebook page, advised customers to use alternative digital channels and mobile applications to continue their banking transactions. Among the recommended platforms are the iRakyat mobile banking application, BRICK, QR2E and the i-bizRAKYAT business banking portal.

items.title: Traffic congestion, several accidents reported on NSE ahead of Deepavali
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic congestion was reported along several major stretches of the North-South Expressway (NSE) from midnight, with several accidents reported ahead of tomorrow's Deepavali celebrations. According to updates by PLUS on X, traffic congestion was first reported at 12.04am along the northbound stretch from Permatang Pauh to Sungai Dua. For southbound traffic, congestion was also reported on the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE) from Bandar Serenia to Bandar Baru Nilai.

items.title: Pas: Why is Najib's house arrest still on hold? [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas has demanded an explanation from the government over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest despite the payment of his RM50 million fine. Its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan questioned why the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) was still seeking clarification on the conditional royal pardon granted nearly two months ago. He said the pardon, announced by the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department on Sept 18, clearly stipulated that Najib could serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the fine.

items.title: Prince Harry seeks to appeal after losing case against UK tabloid
items.summary: LONDON: Prince Harry on Friday launched a legal challenge after losing a privacy case against the publisher of the British tabloid the Daily Mail. The High Court in August ordered Harry and six others, including pop legend Elton John, to make an initial payment of £9.5 million (US$13 million) to Associated Newspapers Limited (ANL) after finding against them a month earlier. Huge costs The court noted that ANL estimated its total costs defending itself had reached about £34.5 million by July 9.

items.title: Keeping the art of kolam alive, one grain at a time [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Grain by grain, Sivabalan Arumugam transforms ordinary rice grains into intricate works of art. With nimble hands, he moves across the floor, bringing vibrant kolam designs to life. For the 36-year-old founder of Life Creation and Design Rangoli Kolam, the temporary nature of his creations has never dampened his passion for the traditional art form.

items.title: Meghan Markle's father arrested in US over child sexual abuse images
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, was arrested on Friday on a charge of possessing child sexual abuse material, including photographs of himself with naked underage girls, found in rented storage units in California. "Mr. Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said in a statement. If convicted, Markle could face up to 20 years in prison, the Justice Department said.

items.title: Paraguayan President Pena impeached over banking crisis
items.summary: ASUNCION: Paraguayan senators on Friday voted to impeach President Santiago Pena over the collapse of a major bank that locked almost half the population out of their accounts and triggered widespread protests. Around three million people have been unable to access their money since the Central Bank took control of Ueno Bank on Tuesday and froze its accounts over concerns about its solvency. A Central Bank official told AFP that advance payments to some affected depositors had begun on Thursday afternoon.

items.title: Deepavali joy amid fading estate life
items.summary: But when Deepavali comes around, the stillness gives way to festive music, brightly lit homes and the crackle of fireworks as children and grandchildren return to celebrate the festival of lights. Born and raised on the estate, Gopal has watched the once-thriving plantation community gradually shrink as families retired, moved away and sought new lives elsewhere. Yet Deepavali remains a cherished occasion, bringing a fleeting return of the warmth and camaraderie that once defined life on the estate.

items.title: Melaka polls: Bersatu welcomes PH despite no pact
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu has not issued any official directive to its grassroots to reciprocate support for Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidates in the Melaka election. Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the party nonetheless welcomed support from any party or voter intending to back its candidates. "We welcome anyone who believes it is good to support Bersatu.

items.title: Azmin: Johor, Negri setbacks won't affect Bersatu in Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA: Bersatu's failure to win seats in the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections does not necessarily reflect voter support for the party in Melaka. Its secretary-general, Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, said the party acknowledged the risks but expected to reduce them through strategic planning and trained machinery. He said the party's decision to contest seven seats was made after weighing various factors through strategic consideration and careful study.

items.title: Cornell rape case exposes MeToo backlash
items.summary: NEW YORK: An allegation of gang rape at the elite Cornell University horrified Americans. The doxxing, threats and harassment targeting the woman, Thomas Giuffra said, expose a wider backlash against the MeToo movement, which prompted a societal reckoning with sexual abuse by men. The lawyer also said he had received death threats.

items.title: Melaka polls: Political canvassing amid a calm facade
items.summary: Campaign workers from Barisan Nasional, Pakatan Harapan and Perikatan Nasional have described the campaign as largely peaceful, with candidates concentrating on meeting voters, visiting communities and presenting their respective agendas. Some have even likened the contest to a friendly football match, suggesting that political differences have yet to translate into open hostility among campaign teams. A campaign worker for BN's Serkam candidate Datuk Azman Abdullah said there had been no provocations, describing the campaign as a healthy contest.

items.title: NST CRIME WATCH: Sexual abuse, brawls and riots make headlines this week [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: At least 26 people were arrested following two riots in the Klang Valley, with police also seizing several weapons. POLICE NAB 26 IN TWO SEPARATE RIOTS KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained 17 people following a brawl at the Lembah Jaya flats in Ampang , after videos of the incident went viral on social media. However, police arrested 17 men from a group that had gathered at the location.

items.title: NST COURT WATCH: Rape acquittal, faith rehabilitation order among key court cases this week [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An acquittal in a rape case, an order to undergo faith rehabilitation, fines for illegal racing under newly amended laws and unsuccessful court bids were among the court cases that made headlines across the country this week. PREACHER DA'I SYED WINS APPEAL Celebrity preacher Da'i Syed, whose real name is Syed Shah Iqmal Syed Mohd Shaiful, was cleared of raping a 23-year-old woman in Shah Alam in 2019. In a 2-1 majority decision, Court of Appeal judges Datuk Azman Abdullah, who chaired the panel, and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid allowed Syed Shah Iqmal's final appeal, while Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid dissented.

items.title: Deepavali or Diwali? The story behind the two names of the Festival of Lights
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — As Malaysians prepare to celebrate Deepavali tomorrow, a linguistic debate about the Festival of Lights still lingers: is it Deepavali or Diwali? Goddess Lakshmi is also worshipped on this day to seek wealth and prosperity. New Year for Gujaratis Interestingly, Deepavali also marks the end of the Gujarati calendar, with the community celebrating the Gujarati New Year, or Bestu Varas, the very next day, according to Shree Lakshmi Narayan Mandir president Rajesh Kamani.

items.title: If Malaysia plans to roll out a new long-term care insurance, what lessons can be learned from Singapore?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — If Malaysia was to introduce its own national insurance for long-term care (especially for older persons), could the Singapore experience be a useful reference? Here’s a quick look at the Singapore government’s national long-term care insurance CareShield Life, provided via its equivalent to Malaysia’s Employees Provident Fund which is the Central Provident Fund (CPF). In 2020, Singapore launched CareShield Life which offers lifelong monthly cash payouts if one becomes severely disabled and needs long-term care.

items.title: Cornell faculty vote no-confidence in leadership over alleged gang rape
items.summary: NEW YORK: Faculty members at Cornell University on Friday passed a no-confidence vote over how the elite college's leadership handled an alleged gang rape that has sparked outcry in the United States. The result is not binding but marks a strong symbolic rebuke of administrators following the 2024 incident, which saw a female student assaulted by seven male students on campus, according to a lawsuit. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Trump elevates hardliner Stephen Miller as chief of staff after midterm defeat
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump named trusted aide Stephen Miller as his chief of staff on Friday, giving the architect of some of his toughest domestic policies one of the most powerful jobs in Washington after Republicans lost control of Congress. Trump said the change would take effect on Monday. A White House official said Miller's appointment signalled that Trump had no intention of rethinking his policies and was instead rewarding his most loyal aides.

items.title: France's top literary prize winner defends 'playful' use of AI
items.summary: PARIS: The winner of France's top literary award, the Prix Goncourt, defended on Friday his "playful", "ironic" and very limited use of AI in his acclaimed book. "It is ridiculously absurd to think for half a second that I used generative AI to write anything at all in this book," Philippe Jaenada said in a statement sent to AFP by his publisher, Flammarion, in which the author detailed how he used the technology. "The playful or ironic use of AI — above all fully acknowledged — was actually part of my plan even before I started writing," he said.

items.title: French death blaze holiday home owner to face trial
items.summary: PARIS: The owner of a French holiday home where 11 people died in a fire in 2023 will face trial for involuntary manslaughter and involuntary bodily harm, prosecutors said on Friday. The victims of the fire in the small town of Wintzenheim in the Alsace region of eastern France were 10 adults with learning disabilities and their companion, on a break during the peak of the French summer holiday season. The holiday home owner and a management company of which she is the sole shareholder will face the charges, Paris prosecutors said.
